name: Water resources planning guideline
fact: Updated 16 June 2026; water companies must prepare and maintain WRMPs and review them annually, with at least five-year plan cycles.
gate: WRMP strategy is company-level supply planning and does not prove spare capacity or a connection offer for a target parcel.

name: Water resources planning guideline detailed guidance
fact: The 2026 guideline covers supply forecasts, demand forecasts, uncertainty, options and best-value planning for secure sustainable water supply.
gate: Forecast headroom or options in a WRMP are not parcel-level capacity reservations.

name: Water resources planning guideline consultation outcome
fact: Updated 8 May 2026; the Environment Agency confirmed the revised planning guidance would proceed after consultation changes.
gate: Consultation outcome governs company planning methodology, not site-specific network capacity.

name: Statutory drainage and wastewater management plan guidelines
fact: Published 20 May 2025; sewerage undertakers have a statutory duty to prepare, publish and maintain Drainage and Wastewater Management Plans under section 94 of the Water Industry Act 1991.
gate: A DWMP is strategic evidence and does not guarantee treatment or sewer headroom at a development site.

name: DWMP guidance purpose and legal terminology
fact: The guidance distinguishes statutory 'must' requirements from recommended 'should' actions and notes the first cycle of DWMPs was published in 2023.
gate: Plan compliance language must not be converted into a site connection approval.

name: Water supply wastewater and water quality planning guidance
fact: Government planning guidance says early engagement with water and sewerage companies can identify infrastructure issues; water supply may matter for large unplanned development or significant connection works.
gate: Early engagement is evidence-gathering, not capacity confirmation or permission.

name: National flood risk standing advice
fact: Updated 28 May 2026; local planning authorities are directed to research site flood risk, assess FRA and SuDS information, and apply sequential/exception-test guidance where relevant.
gate: Flood-zone screening is not a complete site-specific flood-risk conclusion.

name: Flood risk assessments planning application guidance
fact: Updated 28 May 2026; applicants must determine when an FRA and sustainable drainage strategy are needed and appraise limitations of existing flood models.
gate: Model or map presence is not a satisfactory FRA and does not prove planning acceptability.

name: Preparing a flood risk assessment standing advice
fact: Updated 28 May 2026; a completed FRA is submitted with the planning application and may be rejected if not satisfactory.
gate: Submission of an FRA is not approval of drainage or planning permission.

name: National standards for sustainable drainage systems
fact: The national non-statutory SuDS standards apply to new development and promote runoff control, flood-risk reduction, water quality, biodiversity and long-term performance.
gate: Compliance design evidence is separate from sewer-company connection capacity or planning consent.

name: Detailed national SuDS standards
fact: Standards cover runoff destination, everyday rainfall, extreme rainfall, water quality, amenity, biodiversity and construction/maintenance integrity.
gate: A compliant concept still requires site-specific design, infiltration evidence and relevant approvals.

name: Surface Water Investment Model approach
fact: Published 18 May 2026; the Environment Agency SWIM approach supports business cases for multiple small SuDS measures and FCERM grant-in-aid appraisal.
gate: A funding appraisal method is not a funded parcel scheme or drainage approval.

name: Water discharge and groundwater activity environmental permits
fact: The Environment Agency collection includes updated 20 April 2026 guidance for surface-water and groundwater discharge permit activities.
gate: Planning permission and environmental discharge permission are separate legal states.

name: Water supply asset discharge consents and permits
fact: Updated 23 June 2026; certain water-supply asset discharges require section 166 consent or an environmental permit and risk assessment.
gate: Water-company infrastructure operation evidence is not development-site discharge consent.

name: Ofwat developers overview
fact: Ofwat explains developer service routes including company-installed connections, requisitioning, self-lay and NAV arrangements.
gate: A market route or statutory duty does not reserve network capacity for a named development.

name: Ofwat measures of experience 2025-2030
fact: The 2025-30 D-MeX framework combines developer-customer satisfaction with levels-of-service metrics for water-company developer services.
gate: Service-performance metrics are not evidence of site capacity or planning readiness.

name: Ofwat measures of experience overview
fact: Updated D-MeX arrangements operate from 1 April 2025 and measure service provided to developers, SLPs, NAVs and new-connection customers.
gate: Customer-service incentives must not be treated as connection approval.

name: Ofwat charging rules update consultation
fact: Ofwat consulted on changes intended for April 2026 to charging rules supporting new appointments and developer-services markets.
gate: Charging-rule changes affect commercial process, not physical network headroom.

name: Ofwat bulk supply agreements for enabling infrastructure
fact: Published 2 February 2026; Ofwat guidance covers bulk-supply agreements enabled by major infrastructure such as reservoirs, treatment, recycling, desalination and transfer networks.
gate: Major infrastructure agreement guidance is not a site-specific supply commitment.

name: National Highways planning and the strategic road network
fact: National Highways is a statutory planning consultee and encourages early advice where development may affect SRN safety, queuing, maintenance, improvement or access.
gate: Proximity to the SRN is not evidence of acceptable access or available junction capacity.

name: National Highways DCO programme of activities
fact: The programme describes initial engagement, options assessment, highway-solution development and DCO examination for third-party NSIPs affecting the SRN.
gate: Process engagement is not highway-solution approval or DCO consent.

name: National Highways route strategies
fact: Route strategies are research inputs to future Road Investment Strategy planning and include route-level challenges and opportunities.
gate: A route-strategy proposal is not a committed scheme or parcel access improvement.

name: National Highways strategic road network initial report
fact: The SRN Initial Report sets proposals and evidence for the third road period and future investment planning.
gate: Investment planning does not guarantee delivery timing or local development mitigation.

name: National Highways Connecting the country
fact: National Highways' 2050 strategy sets long-term customer and network themes for the SRN.
gate: Long-term strategy is not site-specific highway capacity or access permission.

name: Thames Water water and wastewater capacity
fact: Thames Water says a pre-planning enquiry checks whether water and wastewater networks have capacity and can provide a planning-support letter; lack of capacity triggers discussion of action and timing.
gate: A pre-planning letter is not planning permission, a connection agreement or a permanent capacity reservation.

name: Thames Water planning your development
fact: The developer planning page separates pipe location, pre-planning capacity, self-lay, works near assets and trade-effluent consent routes.
gate: Discovery of a relevant service route does not prove technical approval.

name: Thames Water new mains or connections
fact: Where development includes new roads or lacks an existing water main, Thames Water requires a new-main and connection process that can be delivered by the company or an accredited SLP.
gate: Need for a new main is an infrastructure requirement, not evidence the site is unserviceable or consented.

name: Thames Water sewers and wastewater developer services
fact: The developer page separates sewer connection, adoption, build-over, diversion, requisition and trade-effluent processes.
gate: Service availability does not imply network capacity or technical acceptance.

name: Thames Water adopting a sewer
fact: New sewers and pumping stations may be offered for adoption under section 104, subject to Code for Adoption, design and legal requirements.
gate: Technical adoption route is separate from planning permission and live sewer headroom.

name: Thames Water developing over or near sewers
fact: Thames Water requires build-over controls near public sewers/lateral drains and generally prefers diversion for new-property conflicts.
gate: A mapped sewer proximity is not exact alignment or build-over permission.

name: Thames Water self-lay overview
fact: Accredited SLPs can perform contestable new-main and connection work under Water Code for Adoption and design standards.
gate: An SLP route changes delivery responsibility, not network-capacity evidence.

name: Thames Water building over public sewers
fact: A build-over agreement is required before relevant construction and applications are technically reviewed; larger sewers can require CCTV, engineer and legal review.
gate: Planning permission does not substitute for a build-over agreement.
